utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you for giving me the floor. I shall be very brief, and I -- I understand that you -- I sought to address you with regard to the latest decision we received on Friday. We wish to expression our concern with the Chamber and say that this is a major blow to the Defence. We also wish to say that the witnesses are not ready to come to The Hague with all that haste, either for the depositions or for the main hearings as viva voce witnesses. Why, Your Honours? One-third of the witnesses have no passports or visas, and it takes time to obtain those. One-third of the witnesses are sick or for health reasons cannot come. And one-third needs to be organised to come, because at no time did we tell them that they had to come to The Hague. From the very beginning, they were on our deposition lists -- depositions list, as you know, and now all that needs to be organised, and it is quite impossible within these seven days. Moreover, Your Honours, the question arises as to the purpose of coming to The Hague for depositions. The Defence is now no longer interested in that. If they have to come to The Hague, then why don't they come to the courtroom and testify in vivo? Because the Defence does not want to lose any witnesses. We believe that that would seriously prejudice our case. There is yet another possibility, Your Honours, for those witnesses who are either ill or have no passports, to organise a videolink for them. But in any event, Your Honours, the Defence needs time to go down there, in that case, and prepare the witnesses, proof the witnesses, and instruct them about all the technical and other details, just as Mr. Stringer had to travel to the United States when they were -- their witnesses were testifying by videolink. Your Honours, my concern is even greater because we think that this institution is a very serious one and perhaps for safety reasons we should go into private session. It is up to you to decide. We do not believe that these reasons changed for five days. We held all the meetings with the head of the security for the Tribunal with all the relevant and honourable officials of this Court, and nobody ever said anything. Quite the contrary, all the checks were done. You know that people went to Mostar, checked it all, Your Honours. In Mostar, there must be -- well, I'm talking perhaps off the top of my head but there must be 100 or 200 of officials of the -- the UNHCR and representatives of this Tribunal. What has happened now at this particular moment, when the witnesses are to give depositions? Is it because Mr. Paddy Ashdown became the High Representative and he was -- he testified in this Tribunal in two cases? Perhaps that has something to do with the change. But in any event, Your Honours, could we at least receive some indication, some instruction? Because within these seven days, or rather until we still have these witnesses who are already here and unless we are done with them, I simply cannot organise anything. I know that this is not your fault. I know that from the very beginning of this case -- and I am grateful to you for your effort to be fair and just, I think that you will show such an effort now, that you will help us somehow. We do hope that we shall find a way to hear those witnesses, and this notification, which says that some safety reasons, security reasons, have arisen now, could we please have this notification or this information? Your Honours, I simply do not believe that news. It must be something else. Something else must be the matter. It has nothing to do with security reasons, and I say that in public for all the world to hear. So could we please see this information or this notification, if possible? Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I shall be very brief. I will not repeat what my colleague has said before me, but I fully agree with everything he said. However, I wanted to add one comment in relation to the -- to our future schedule, because the Defence's work was closely related to, connected with, the visit to Mostar, because Mr. Martinovic's Defence wanted to use that time, because these are all witnesses for Mr. Krsnik, and it will be enough for only one of us to be present there, and the other two members of our team and our investigators would seize this precious time to carry out final preparations for our witnesses so that they could -- so that we could take over only a couple of days after the end of the depositions, and that was why we asked for the break. However, in view of this new situation, this situation where we are not going to Mostar, this Defence will - and I have to say it straight away - this Defence will make a new application, that is that when Mr. Krsnik finishes, and of course it now depends whether the witnesses will be coming here to testify or whether he will give up from calling those witnesses who were envisioned for the depositions to after, we shall apply for a short break after that, because that time which we thought we would spend in Mostar to carry out the final preparations for our case and for the organisation of witnesses, now we shall have to ask for a break, a short one, the shortest possible, and I also believe that the practice of this Tribunal has been -- has been so far that a short break for the second accused has always been approved after the Defence of the first accused has completed its case. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that this Chamber was greatly shocked by the news that we have to give up the deposition in Mostar at that late hour. So we very much sympathise with the Defence team, with their situation they are now in. As you understand, this Trial Chamber has invested great efforts in this aspect. We instructed the Registrar and a representative from this Chamber to make a field inspection, and we acted in accordance with the report they filed to this Chamber. In other words, this Trial Chamber has made superhuman efforts to accommodate the request from the Defence team. So that's why we said that we are greatly shocked by this news and we have to change everything we have done in the past. So in this aspect, first, I will promise Mr. Krsnik that we will furnish the memos filed by the security section or Registrar on the security situation in this aspect. Secondly, this Trial Chamber will do everything possible to help the Defence case -- to help the Defence team to facilitate its representation of their case in this aspect. So if there are any requests from the Defence team, we would like to consider them after the filing. I believe this is all I could say at this stage. So could we have the -- yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. Now I will not bother you any more. I merely wish to thank you, Mr. President, and Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good weekend in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start today? We won't keep you long. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Speaking of not keeping this witness long, Your Honour, I believe the Prosecution has already used more time than the Defence did on direct, Madam Registrar is going to check that. We were wondering how much time will be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we believe that the Prosecution is doing its utmost and trying to facilitate the proceedings in this case. Mr. Scott. Could I ask you how long you are going to take for your further cross-examination this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would hope with responsive answers to the witness could complete my cross-examination in about 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Scott. Cross-examined by Mr. Scott: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to pick up from Friday before we move forward, I think we all understand that at some point in approximately early October of 1993, you came, took a senior position in the 3rd Brigade and then later in early 1994 you took a senior position in the 2nd Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know if these questions might tend to identify so perhaps out of caution we should go to private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I understand your testimony from Friday, you were no longer involved or a member of either the HVO components of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina army or of the Republic of Croatia army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand, what time are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- the current time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am neither a member of the Croat Defence Council or the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how are you engaged in business or how you support yourself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, do we have to go to the private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I suppose out of caution we could. I didn't know depending on the nature that it was just a general business matter it might not be so identifying but out of an abundance of caution, we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, two things, at first, I was shocked that so much time is granted I really do not know when I will finish my witnesses because I thought that Mr. Scott would out of sheer decency say 25 minutes not 45 minutes, and the second thing that shocks me that under the guise of questioning credibility, these questions are asked. I don't see the relevance of questions, what is this witness's livelihood, how does he make his livelihood. I would be the happiest if I could answer this question. What does it have to do with this case and what is the relevance of that particular question? How does this witness now make a livelihood to this case? Could the Prosecutor please analyse a little bit his rights, the rights that he has in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as first issue, I believe that the Prosecution has promised us to finish his cross-examination in 45 minutes if he will get the proper answer from this witness. We believe that is bona fide gesture so his request is granted. At the second issue, this Chamber are also interested in hearing the answer of this question. So we'll go to the private session, please. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours and the purposes of the record we would like to object to the procedure whereby the Prosecution gets much more time on cross than direct and we want a continuing objection for the record, a contemporaneous objection so that at some point in the future it will not be said that we did not contemporaneously object to this procedure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your objection is registered in the transcript. We will take into consideration of our objections when we are allocating time to the Prosecution for the cross-examination in the future time. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a man named Milan Kovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean Mr. Kovac, a representative in the parliament of the Republic of Croatia, is that the person you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How do you know him, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from Herzegovina, from Posusje, which is a neighbouring municipality and I am, as you know, from Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he considered one of the persons, one of the Herzegovinians who continues to be in favour of a separate Croat entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whom you mean, when you say that somebody advocated Herzegovina as a separate part of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Not even the Croatian community never denied the attributes of statehood of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Croatian people at the referendum in 1992 opted for an integral Bosnia and Herzegovina. So Mr. Prosecutor, your allegation is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, not going back to the 1992 referendum, isn't it correct, sir, that at least a faction of the HDZ political party in Bosnia-Herzegovina led by Ante Jelavic, involving you as well, isn't it true that at least a faction of the HDZ party has continued to work for and promote and seek the establishment of a separate Croat entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the last several years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll come back to that. Sir, have you been involved in any efforts, groups or meetings, in connections with defending Mr. Naletilic against the charges here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. What meetings do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of any organisations or groups that have been formed or that have evolved for the purpose of assisting Mr. Naletilic's Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from coming here to testify, sir, have you ever been involved in any efforts discussions or meetings for the purposes of promoting and assisting the Defence of Mr. Naletilic against the charges here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say to this Honourable Court that there are no organised groups, there are people who sit down, who reminisce on those war days and they just engage in friendly conversations. There are no organised groups as such, in the way you imply, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber when you were first contacted by anyone in connection with Mr. Naletilic's Defence team about testifying here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time somebody contacted me -- do you mean my testimony here before this Court?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Any time that you were initially contacted about giving testimony on behalf of the Defence in this case. When did that take place and who contacted you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik asked me whether I knew anything about 1992, what happened at the time, and whether I would be willing to testify, and I said I would. And that I would be willing to say everything I know, and that could assist this Honourable Court to arrive at objective information and at the truth, and as such, I have placed myself at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just the other part of my question, can you give your best estimate approximately of when that first contact was made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was a year ago roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir I'm trying to be very careful not to ask you to identify your position. But you did make a -- you were at this gathering and during a speech that you made at that gathering, sir, didn't you refer to Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, as "the famous commander of the legendary Convicts Battalion"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that particular speech of mine. I don't remember what I said at the 3rd anniversary of the guard's brigade but I did say to this Honourable Court that the Convicts Battalion was one of the units that served as a foundation for the development of the 2nd Brigade of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you not refer to Mr. Naletilic as the "famous commander" of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that for a fact. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could the witness be shown the second bundle of documents that were distributed on Friday? And Exhibit -- I direct the witness's attention, please, to Exhibit 936.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor, I don't see Exhibit 936.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me see if we can assist you. My apologies, Your Honour, apparently Madam Registrar, it was apparently placed at the end of the first bundle so in this instance, Exhibit 936 should be at the end of the first bundle of documents that was used on Friday. Mr. President, for obvious reasons perhaps I'll ask that it not be placed on the ELMO so as not to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could look at Exhibit 936, and you have the full Croatian language version in front of you, first of all, and again without identifying yourself, and this document will have to be under seal but does not the first page of that -- of this document include a photograph of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And directing your attention to the very last paragraph of the document, in addition to talking about Slobodan Praljak and others, is it not there where you are reported to have said, described quote, "The famous commander of the legendary Convicts Battalion, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot allow such things in the Croatian text, can we please take a look at what it says? This -- these are journalists words, this is the journalist who concludes, and says this, in the last paragraph of the Croatian text. Will you allow me? At the end, let's say that the representatives of the brigade, so the representatives of the brigade, handed over, seized rifles as a souvenir and a war trophy, as a souvenir, for the days spent together in memory of the days spent during -- on front lines and to the Colonel Slobodan Praljak, to the general major Miljenko Lasic and the famous commander of the legendary Convicts Battalion, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Where does it say here that the witness mentioned this commander in his speech? Again, what is Mr. Prosecutor engaging in when he asks his question? It would have been fair of him to have said, "Did you hand over the guns to Mr. Naletilic?" But these are the words of the journalist. These are not the words of my witness. And this is as clear as a bell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think the Prosecution was asking a question to this witness. This witness has the full right to deny any allegations, no matter put by the Prosecution or by journalists in this article. Let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask a couple of follow-up questions to clarify, Witness, in light of the comments made. Were you present -- are you suggesting or did you understand that some sort of special firearms or awards or gifts were given to Mr. Praljak, Mr. Lasic and Mr. Tuta at this event? Is that what we should understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were no special awards or decorations. These were rifles which were given to them in memory of the days spent together on the front -- during the war, and they were handed over to the aforementioned gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And at the time that these firearms or weapons were awarded to Mr. Praljak, Mr. Lasic and Mr. Naletilic, when it was presented to Mr. Naletilic, was he indeed described when being handed and presented these weapons, was he indeed described as the famous commander of the legendary Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, these are the journalist's words, and as far as I know, when these were handed over, no descriptions were given. The names were called and the gifts were given to them, and that was the way the procedure went. There were no big words said about the people. And as to what the journalist wrote in here, that was his view of the things, and that was the way he expressed himself on the paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir, we have to move on to try to finish as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness please be shown or assisted with Exhibit P926?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, as you look at the Croatian version of this document, you said a few moments ago, sir, that you deny the existence of any movement or effort to create a separate Croat entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina but sir, is it not true that in fact there have been a number of efforts and steps take to do that, including a declaration of something called the Croat national congress, in this particular instance dated the 28th of October, 2000? You're familiar with that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the session of the Croatian National Parliament or Sabor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the President on the 28th of that organisation or group on the 28th of October, 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: What organisation do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croat National Congress?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the Croatian National parliament [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, isn't it correct that Mr. Jelavic was removed as the Bosnian Croat member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina by the Office of the High Representative for his anti-Dayton activities in continuing to promote the creation of a separate Croat entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante -- Mr. Ante Jelavic was elected at the democratic elections, and he was legitimately elected by the Croatian people. He enjoyed almost 95 per cent support of the Croatian people, and the Croatian people was embittered by the decision of the High Representative, and the part of the international administration in Bosnia and Herzegovina about abolishing institutional rights of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [no interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We don't get any interpretation. Could you please repeat it once again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really don't know where we are headed with this cross-examination. What is the relevance? This is what happened in 2001. But what I said already a long time ago, I'm very interested in the position of my learned friend. Who does he advocate here? Who does he Prosecutor here? We are talking here about the political struggle about a democratic struggle that many is taking place in two entities, one is the federation, the other is the Republika Srpska. I'm very shocked. I see these decisions by the High Representative for the first time and I believe Your Honours will also be interested in how decisions are made in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Somebody is referring to the constitutional order of the federation. The federation does not have a constitutional order. The only entity that has a constitutional order is Bosnia and Herzegovina and the federation is just one unit of the whole state and the other entity is Republika Srpska. I don't see the purpose of my learned friend's examination. Does he begrudge the Croat people their struggle, their fight for democracy? I said a long time ago that here he acts as an advocate, as a -- rather than a Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think the Prosecution is entitled to ask any question which is relevant to this case, and I believe that the question asked by the Prosecution in this question, in this particular circumstances, is related to the credibility of this witness. Let us hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you will allow me, I apologise. Your Honours, what is the relevance when this witness says that in the federation, which is 70-30 ratio in favour of Muslims when he says that the Croats are deprived of their rights? But what does that have to do with this case? What is the relevance? What is the relevance of the year 2001 and the -- where as the indictment refers to the year 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you have to understand that we have the witness here. I could not explain in detail how we see this question is relevant to this case. Your objection is correctly registered in the transcript and we will allow the Prosecution to move on and at a later stage, when we evaluate the evidence, the testimony given by this witness, we will take your objections into consideration. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, because of the time, I'm simply going to have -- so the witness knows I'm referring to and the Chamber, simply going to have to ask the witness please be shown Exhibit P876.06. Which is -- which includes or is included in that exhibit a copy of the official decision of the Office of the High Representative referring -- removing Mr. Jelavic and others, and because of time, Mr. President, I don't have time to go through that document with specific questions but I think the document for these purposes will largely, I hope, speak for itself. Perhaps the Chamber will have questions, Judges questions, about the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, whether you agree with it or not, isn't it true that on March the 7th, 2001, the Office of the High Representative removed Mr. Jelavic from his position as the Croat member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina? I realise you may not agree with that but it's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Jelavic was removed by the High Representative, but I apologise, was I maybe supposed to have a Croatian version of this document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That particular document -- excuse me, witness, there is no translation at this time, for which I apologise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I haven't got it from the Prosecution. I don't have it at all. This Exhibit 876.06, I haven't got it in my bundle. It may be an accident but I do not have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's in the second bundle of documents furnished by the Prosecution on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we all have it. I think there must be some mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We believe that it's there, Mr. President, if some reason one was left out of one of the bundles we will certainly correct that. Apparently everybody else in the courtroom has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't have it. I checked a hundred times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll provide it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you have to provide.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course, and every other bundle seems to have it but we'll provide it again to Mr. Krsnik, surely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on the -- again I'm going to ask you a similar question hopefully I ask you not to identify yourself but were you also involved in a gathering or proceeding involving the anniversary and an oath taking ceremony of the 2nd Guards Brigade on approximately the 5th of June, 1994?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the witness can please be shown Exhibits P775.2? It should be, I hope, the first document in the second bundle, P775.2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document has not been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The witness is right, Your Honour, I'll have to ask the assistance of the interpreters before a translation can be provided for the record. But what I would like the translator's assistance on, please, the assistance of the interpretation booth, just simply going to read it to you for the purposes of framing the question, sir. Directing the translation booth's attention to the part, the bottom part of the first page where it says "the only different tune."

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a procedural matter here. Your Honours ruled last October that the Prosecution could not introduce or attempt to introduce any documents against our clients, the accused, unless they had been previously translated into a language which they understood. After I think was it November 10th or 11th, and now the Prosecution is doing exactly that, they are violating this Trial Chamber's order. Our clients have not been able to read these documents because they do not speak English, they do not read English and I object strongly and I will keep objecting strongly to this procedure. The accused has different rights than the Prosecution does. We all know that, and this Trial Chamber entered the ruling last October, no documents could be attempted to be introduced against the accused unless they had been previously translated into a language that they understand. And these documents have not, Your Honour. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Mr. Meek, on this point. First of all, we believe that all the documents tendered have to be translated into the language that the accused understand. As for the specific contents of this document, first, I'm not quite sure this document is directly -- criminalise your clients in certain points. Secondly, this is cross-examination. I think the Prosecution is going to ask a very simple question concerning with the certain paragraph or certain sentence of this document, which the interpreters in the booths will help us, I hope. Thirdly, if the Prosecution wants to tender this document into evidence, the translation shall be furnished as soon as possible. Mr. Scott, are you going to extensively use this document or just put one question concerning with one paragraph of this document to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I hope to put one, as far as possible, I hope, to put one question to the witness based on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed but if you want to tender this document, you ever to furnish us with the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can actually if I can have the assistance to put the document, the statement in full context lest there be some concern raised about that. If I can ask assistance of the interpreter in the paragraph starting "although inspiring." If I can read it perhaps we can get the translation. "Although inspiring a normal degree of proudness of Croat Herzegovina according to the instant translation by our interpreter, all speeches were very moderate and not directed against Muslims or the recent political decisions. The soldiers were asked to understand that the politicians were doing the best possible job, although people and soldiers did not always like the decisions at first. The army was there to defend those decisions and executes orders. This was stated by both politicians and military leaders." Obviously in the next section I will not refer to the name. "The only different tune was heard at the last speech made by, and I leave that, the record, what is stated in the exhibit, who made a much more violent speech delivered in the Nazi style of the 30s mainly directed against the Chetniks, even spoke of the necessity to cross the Drina. The monitor observed that after the parade he was publicly greeted by another officer with a Nazi salute." Now, based on that, sir, do you remember giving such a speech and receiving such a salute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I regret that such information is presented here in this Court. I never greeted anyone, nor did anyone greet me, with a Nazi salute. Quite the contrary. I condemn any Naziism and this allegation of the Prosecutor is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were removed from your position in the HVO component of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the stabilisation force, otherwise known as SFOR; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was suspended, I'm sorry, I was suspended by SFOR and removed by the Croat member of the Presidency at the time, and the reason was I helped to put out the fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the standard procedure of the commander of the SFOR directed at the parties in the area was fully observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, weren't the reasons given by SFOR that you were involved in the unauthorized movement of HVO soldiers to Croatia and because of your involvement in partisan HDZ politics which was inconsistent with a professional military position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true that at the time I was politically active or involved in party politics. That is simply not true. However, at that time, at this time, throughout that time that we are talking about, it is true that there were those branches of the old system of the former communist intelligence community which existed in all three sides, in the Muslim and Croat and Serb side, the so-called counterintelligence service, that is KOS, or UDB, and it is quite obvious that these services tried to prejudice, tried to discredit, tried to undermine and so that a number of such information was out of place, but that is how they removed everybody who was in their way, who they thought should be discredited and needless to say, the international community in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time absorbed a large part of that information and practically, unfortunately, took decisions and made moves in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina based on such information. On the other hand, I also need to point out before this Honourable Court that I have cooperated fantastically well with SFOR officers, with SFOR commanders, with generals who conducted MPRI programme, Crosby Senton and General Carl Vaughan, that I was commended on several occasions by generals who were in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're telling this Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we go into private session? Why is it so difficult? The Prosecutor is asking questions and will Mr. Prosecutor please take note of this? Because he knows he will get an answer which will disclose the identity and secondly we need these names in the transcript the Prosecutor needs to repeat the question so that the names of the generals with whom the witness cooperated can be put in because we do not have a single name of the -- of any SFOR general or any other international organisations in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, the commanders of the SFOR is a fact. I believe that the interpreters will check with all those names at a later stage. It's a fact. Everybody knows about the names of the SFOR commanders. Yes, Mr. Scott, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, perhaps out of an abundance of caution we should go to private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a few brief questions. Unfortunately, those questions are to my mind not relevant at all but I have to because of the last questions put by the Prosecution to discredit the witness. Re-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the last few questions with regard to the removals, the actions by the High Representative, I had a feeling that you did not have the opportunity to explain all the circumstances of these events, and as you may have noticed, Mr. Prosecutor wanted to discredit you by advocating one political option, that is Bosniak option, against the Croatian political option in the year 2001, i.e. 2002. Therefore, I would kindly ask you to explain to the Honourable Court -- can we please go to private session? Because I'm sure that the witness will -- actually he has to reveal his identity, if he wants to reply to my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, the elections were general parliamentary elections and they took place on the 11th of November, 2001. The election law, the so-called Berry Elections Law which was detrimental for the Croatian people because it left room for the Croatian members to be elected by that -- somebody else could decide about the election of the Croatian representative at the highest level. If we know that such an election model, and with regard to the fact that the parliament consisted of two chambers at the level of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that it has 140 seats, Croats would receive some 30 seats, would be entitled to some 30 seats in the parliament. So that at any moment, the majority of votes is against them. The second Chamber, the Chamber of Peoples, which served as a correction to the other Chamber, for checks and balances, and the composition of that other Chamber was 30 Croats, 30 Muslims, 30 Serbs, according to this election model, and with regard to the fact that the federation consists of ten cantons, and according to this allocation that the cantons were given for the election into the Chamber of Peoples, I know for a fact that some members of the international community at the time were asked in the Gorazde canton to declare themselves as Croats of Muslim religion so that they could -- so as to exert influence on the composition of the Croatian part of the parliament so that the 30 seats that -- meant that they could not have 15 plus 1 seats, which would have entitled them to the right of a veto on the decisions passed by the lower Chamber. These precedents resulted in the situation that the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina found themselves in a very complex position, and as such, we voted in the elections on the 11th of November, and the Croatian people and all of its institutions felt threatened as a political people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they felt that their -- they are being led into a position of a minority, of a national minority, and the Washington Agreement, the Dayton Accords, and all the agreements signed in Bosnia-Herzegovina clearly say that Croats are one of the three state-forming peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In such circumstances, in the elections, the Croatian people opted and gave its full support to the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us the percentage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: 95 per cent of the votes at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina, at the level of the federation it was 85 per cent. And at the cantonal level, at the level of counties, 75 to 80 per cent. After that, some people were removed from the election lists, which meant that some people were deprived of their basic human rights, the right to elect and to be elected, the right to work, according to us, according to me personally, according to some intellectuals that I had spoken with, our precedents in the democratic world or at least when it comes to the principles of democracy advocated by the international community for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us what happened, who made the decision, what kind of a decision that resulted in that removal? The elections are now over. What happened next, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: The High Representative, Mr. Wolfgang Petritsch made a decision on the suspension of the Croatian member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is Mr. Ante Jelavic. Mr. Ivo Andric-Luzanski was also removed, Mr. Marko Tokic as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not mention any names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were vice-presidents of the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise for interrupting again, I don't -- I would like to ask you to say -- to explain to the Honourable Court how many people were removed and were the elections over and were these same people elected at the democratic elections? They were elected they were just about to start discharging their duties but the High Representative removed them despite the fact that they had been elected at the democratic elections; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It arises from this that the basic human rights were taken away from some people and that the Croatian people are now being reduced to a national minority, and when we add to that the fact, recently I have read a statement by General Sylvester, the commander of SFOR, who says that the mission of SFOR and the international community in Bosnia-Herzegovina is to form a Bosnian nation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean, a Bosnian nation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that everything is unified, centralised, that one language is replaces all the other languages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that all the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina should Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be called Bosniaks? Bosnians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that contrary to all the international agreements starting with the Washington Agreement, the Dayton Accords?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, because all the -- in all the agreements, Bosnia and Herzegovina consists of the three state-forming peoples and other peoples who live in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I believe that we have provided the Chamber with an explanation. Just two more brief questions. Can you tell us how often have you been in Mostar in the last year or so? Was that every day or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Recently, I have been to Mostar a bit less frequently and previously I was there very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many international representatives live in Mostar? Where do they live? And has there been any incident in the past year or so in the city of Mostar, any incident whatsoever? I'm asking you this question which is beyond the context but I believe that the President will be interested in the situation in Mostar. He said so himself. We have just recently been furnished with a decision saying that Mostar is not a safe place. Has anything happened in the Mostar making it not a safe place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing has happened that would involve the international community, the situation in Mostar, in the safety respect, is okay. It is good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, have you ever spoken to anybody from the circles? How many representatives of the international community live in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly but there is the command of the multi-national division southeast. Its headquarters are in Ortijes and there are other institutions, High Representative, RC, all the other institutions which are in Mostar. I believe that there are no safety problems there. And there is -- there are no, not in any way jeopardised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question. Can we please move to private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from Judges? Judge Clark? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I wonder if I could ask you a few questions about the Convicts Battalion? Do I understand your evidence correctly, when you say or I understand you to say, that the Convicts Battalion comprised of only one unit and one unit only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Convicts Battalion was one unit and its military post code was 1717.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the post code. I'm saying are you saying that the Convicts Battalion consisted of a unit which was stationed in Siroki Brijeg and it had no other associated units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You say that the connection between the unit, I'm being careful now, that you subsequently joined and which was formed, the connection between that unit and the Convicts Battalion was merely that a number of soldiers who had served with the Convicts Battalion transferred to the new unit, the Baja Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Baja Kraljevic had some ten soldiers amongst which -- amongst whom me, who formed this new unit Baja Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And was the leader of that unit known as "Lija"? Was that his nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Predrag Mandic, "Lija," of the Baja Kraljevic unit, who is commander he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could you tell me who actually appointed him commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was appointed by, according to the mobilisation development, it was either the ministry o the Main Staff or it was the presidency, as the signatory of that appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean by presidency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna, the Main Staff probably issued proposals, sent them to the Ministry of Defence, and then the level which was the signatory of the establishment of the unit, I can't exactly remember, but that is the chain, the chain, and that shows how decisions were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You described a few days ago when you were first giving your testimony that the Convicts Battalion was founded by a number of people, and you named the people, and included in that group of five or six people was Mr. Naletilic. The question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The question I want to ask you is why is the Convicts Battalion so associated with Mr. Naletilic in the minds of so many people? Because we've heard evidence that media reports following the recapture, if -- or the liberation of Mostar, in newspaper, radio, television, eulogised Mr. Naletilic and clearly identified him as the hero of the Convicts Battalion. If he was one of many founders, why is the Convicts Battalion, do you know, so associated with Mr. Naletilic to the exclusion of others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of founders, but it is within the context of a team of people who were jointly motivated to defend right from wrong, good from evil, that was at the time imposed on Croats, I mean the evil, so the inevitable answer was to set up a volunteer unit, to provide the necessary answer to this evil which was very near Siroki Brijeg, and if that team worked, then I suppose Mr. Naletilic was seen as a man who had absorbed this libertarian spirit of the west and who therefore showed more courage, more boldness at particular moments, to make the brave step right at the time, and to liberate the bordering areas of the municipality of Siroki Brijeg, and as such, the Convicts Battalion joined in the bloody war and participated with all the other units in the liberation of Mostar, and repulsed that evil which was manifested in the then-reservists Serb, and Montenegrin, the then so-called Yugoslav Army, to repulse them to the areas further away from Mostar and when key facilities from taken, which occupied, dominating positions around the city of Mostar, and from these victories at that time arose in the people's perception and the public opinion the image of Mr. Naletilic as a man who had played a very important role in the liberation of Mostar and that part of Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I don't think anybody denies that that has been the evidence of nearly everybody, that Mr. Naletilic played a huge role, but the question I'm asking you is: Do you know why the Convicts Battalion is forever associated with Mr. Naletilic to the exclusion of all others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said, and that he is one of those men, that he was probably a more ingenious person, a more creative person than other people who were his interlocutors on this team, and he probably set the tone. I mean the -- he provided the initiative, the creative spirit, because each one of those men, as far as I know them, those men lack this particular trait, the initiative, the entrepreneurial spirit. Perhaps they are very good interlocutors for instance, in things when you say, "Yes, let's do that, for instance." But then somebody else has to say, has to decide, right, we'll do this and that on that particular date and in that particular way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So would you accept, then, sir, that Mr. Naletilic was the dominant force in the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was perceived as a man of initiative, because based on my experience, my war experience, I know that people who showed initiative, who were brave and courageous, they were all recognisable as such, and they were perceived as such and they were trusted by the troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Mr. President. Witness, it seems to me that you said that Mladen Naletilic left his post of the commander of the Convicts Battalion in October 1992. I'd like to know why. And in order to take up what other position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I think that Mr. Naletilic quit the position of the commander of the Convicts Battalion in either September or October, 1992, and all of us who were there and worked together and acted together knew even before that Mr. Naletilic had a serious pulmonary lung complaint, and that at that time he used to say that a certain number of leaders had already taken shape in all those combat and liberation operations around the city of Mostar, and that a team had already stood out with the traits of courage, valiance, sufficient integrity and ingeniousness, sufficing to begin to lead the Convicts Battalion. And he withdrew. Whether he went to the municipal staff to some post there, or to the municipal hall in Siroki Brijeg, I believe that he was the deputy mayor of Siroki Brijeg for a while, and in that capacity, he always showed concern for the dead, for the wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who replaced him after he left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mario Hrkac. That was our impression. We thought that he was a natural soldier. One of the soldiers who proved himself during the operations, a supreme fighter, Supreme Commander, and whom people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for the description of Mr. Mario but who appointed him? Who appointed him as Naletilic's successor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I think it was the municipal staff, and then following up the hierarchical ladder that I've already mentioned, the Main Staff, the ministry, following up that ladder. And that is how he came to hold that position. But naturally there was also Mr. Andabak there too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm sorry, you talk about the municipal staff. Who appoints a commander of a battalion? And you also speak about the ministry. You should give me -- you should tell me not a thing but you should give me a positive answer. If you do not know, then you do not know but don't tell me that you think that it was the municipal staff or the ministry who appointed Mr. Naletilic's successor as the commander of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, what I'm saying, Your Honours, I'm saying this because when I cast my mind back to 1992, at that time, those municipal staffs played a dominant role. And as for official appointments, I think that by and large, there were none, but somehow, what was done at that time, when I cast my mind back and when I think about that, and then from that perspective, it is possible that the municipal staff did its bit, but the -- that was the hierarchical ladder, the Main Staff, the ministry, they were the ones who proposed names and who appointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I do not have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges' questions? Yes, Mr. Krsnik? Further examination by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe I only have one question arising from Judge Clark's questions. Was Mr. Ludvig Pavlovic one of the founders of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us how did he end up, and does he also -- has he also become a legendary figure? Is he a charismatic person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is a charismatic person in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question, and I'm very happy that Their Honours asked those questions because I did not want to do that, on purpose, tell us, if basically from the time when the Convicts Battalion was founded, until its end, who was in truth its genuine commander and who were the operative commanders, that is commanders on the ground, in the field, I mean between October 1992 until November 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operative commander was Mario Hrkac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: After him, it was Zeljko Vukoja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there operative men, those who go to the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander basically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is from the foundation until the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was there from day one until the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question, are you aware that Mr. Andabak was on insulin at that time, regularly, every day, at that time. I'm not asking about a later time as a grave diabetic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that he was very gravely suffering from diabetes and that he had to be administered insulin every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, that is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I want to be completely transparent about this I would have a couple of questions related on Mr. Krsnik's re-direct and only I would ask those questions only if allowed to cover that. Not arising from Judge's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, I think we give you the opportunity to ask questions only out of Judges's questions. If there is some questions you are going to ask which is related to just Judges's questions, that is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, as I said I wanted to be fully transparent about that and if that's the case, I have no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Judge Clark? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Arising out of that it's a question I've been anxious to know the answer to for a long time and you appear to be the appropriate person. Maybe you know. Is in Ivan Andabak still alive? And if so, where is he? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Andabak is alive and I believe he is in Slavonia, in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think we've all been curious about him for a while. He's alive and well, I take it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there is no questions out of this question. I have to put an end. Thank you, Witness, for coming here to give your evidence. We appreciate it very much. When the usher pulls down the blinds, she will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the witness is being out, may I say that I'm happy you asked that question. I know that you joined us later, that you did not attend Status Conferences and perhaps I should tell you to read parts of the transcripts of the Status Conferences while Her Honour Judge Wald was there. I do not want to waste time. There were very interesting dialogues between me and the Prosecution because the Prosecution conducted that interview with Mr. Andabak in a very incorrect way, but they removed him from all the witness lists, that is he was arrested and brought for an interview with the Prosecutor, but I merely drawing your attention to those transcripts and I'm very happy that you asked that question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it's not proper, first, without my permission, you make that statement. Secondly, we still have the witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I'm sorry, Your Honours. It will not happen again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I have some exhibits to give to Madam Registrar. Your Honour, Mr. President, I've just learned today that the -- that Defence counsel -- excuse me. Just learned at the break, Your Honours, that tomorrow at 1.30, Defence counsel have a meeting with the Registrar, with security, Mr. Rhode and other members which will address some concerns Defence counsel has and have had for sometime and I would just ask if it would be possible if you would consider allowing us to break at 1.25 tomorrow so that this Defence counsel team and Mr. Seric and Mr. Par, I believe we are all very interested in attending that meeting. Perhaps we could take one 15 minute break instead after half hour break. We would very much like to attend that meeting tomorrow. That's all I'm bringing to your attention, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for informing us about that but this Trial Chamber has not been informed there is a meeting. If there is any, we'll break early to allow you to attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any documents to tender at this stage? And what about the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, it would assist the Prosecution if you would allow us again given past practice to sort through the documents actually used and deal with it on paper, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, but you have to do it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think we only have one new document, and I believe it's D1/390 and perhaps D1/107. I think that's already been submitted. I believe the other exhibits we use were merely photographs and a Prosecution exhibit P704. I believe that's all we would ask to tender into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We believe that we have to make a decision concerning the admission of those documents at a later stage. Mr. Krsnik, are you ready for your next witness? At this moment, I have to tell you that we haven't been furnished with the list of witnesses. So we don't know who will be the next witness yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise but then I must tick off my co-counsel because this should have been done a long time ago. We supplied this list last week both for my learned friends and for you and I do believe that we filed the definitive list. My apologise, Your Honours. Could we go into private session, please so that I can give you the name of the witness and the pseudonym we are proposing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper that the usher is showing to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, you may sit down, please. Mr. Krsnik, we will make a break at 15 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. You are very kind. Examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, first see if that is your name on this sheet of paper. Don't read it aloud, just say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We shall all be addressing you as Witness NN. It is for your protection. Please mind that in your answers, try not to disclose your identity. If you see that in answering a question that might disclose your identity please request a private session because that is what we can do, and then next time, please find the exact speed at which you should answer, not too slow and not too fast. I know that is not easy because you are not often in this position, but you see we have to take care, the interpretation here is of vital importance and we have interpretation into two languages so will you please be cooperative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And let us start off immediately. I will tackle only one year, 1993. Perhaps by way of introduction, just a little bit, we may do something earlier than that, if need be, but basically we shall be talking only about 1993 and we shall be referring to just one event. Will you please make your answers as concise, as concrete as possible so that we can move on? So will you please tell something about your court -- about your self to the Court without giving us your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I was born on the 23rd of August, 1956 in Doljani, municipality of Jablanica. I completed my elementary education in Polog, municipality of Mostar, the secondary school I completed in Mostar. I studied electrical engineering and read it in Split. I graduated in 1980 and at that time, I began to work for Unis in Sarajevo. After that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can follow this dot. You see on the screen. If you can follow that dot, and if you see when it stops. When it stops, then start.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do not tell us these things because we are in open session. This is the first time, you see, don't give you the offices that you held unless we go into private session, first. This will be redacted. Yes, I'll take care.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: After that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps Your Honours, perhaps because these are particulars so perhaps we should go into private session just in case, thank very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The situation was extremely grave for us, the Croats, because we were a minority due to a very large influx of refugees and certain political decisions which were at that time taken in the municipality of Jablanica itself and that was the appointment of Dr. Safet Cibo of the Presidency of the war Presidency of those three municipalities, that is Jablanica, Konjic and Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware who appointed him, it was a lawful decision, a lawful way and whether the relations between the Croats and Bosniaks changed and how? Again just in so many words so the first question is who appointed Dr. Cibo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Dr. Cibo was appointed by Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, and when he came, he wasn't alone. A large number of units came to the municipality of Jablanica. I mean Zuka's units as far as I know. Then some "swans," BH Army units came and they took areas in the municipality of Jablanica itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please slow down? I'm sorry that I am interrupting you but I will have to do it otherwise Judge Diarra has to wait for the interpretation into French from English, so it slows down matters. Will you please slow down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: When he came, those units take the territories and the situation drastically changed at our expense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please just repeat which are the units which came with -- at the same time as Dr. Cibo because they are not in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I know that Zuka came, then some kind of "swans," Suad Alic's Brigade from Konjic with their tanks came and they moved around the town and at the same time, some procurative measures were applied against Croats which did not exist before, that is goods were confiscated from Croat shops, areas were taken from Croats, at checkpoints the control was stepped up and the plates were being removed and practically the freedom of movement was restricted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what month was that when Dr. Cibo arrived and whether that was a lawful decision or whether that was a decision that was imposed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: It was not a lawful appointment for a very simple reason. I know there was a huge resistance by the then Muslim authorities in Jablanica to his arrival and his appointment. Nijaz Ivkovic, the then-president of the municipality of Jablanica personally warned me and told me that the HVO would no longer be able to exist in Jablanica as soon as Mr. Safet Cibo arrived. And his arrival was sometime at the beginning of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's talk about some specific events because we've heard a lot about these things already. Where was your place of work? Did you go there every day? Did something change in that respect, if it did, when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I did not expect that the witness's testimony is going into details. So if you need, Mr. Krsnik, we could go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: See, Witness, even I forget. We have to protect your identity, I know that you're focused on the answers rather than on not revealing your identity, however, whenever you speak either about yourself or your family, ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go into private session, indeed, because this gentleman is easily identifiable in the small -- in the small midst where he lives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please now you have to be careful, make sure you do not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. reveal your identity, if you want to go to private session, we will do that. Did anybody else have their headquarters in that house besides the Mijat Tomic Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: No, nobody else but the civilian components of the HVO, which subsequently was organised there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What went on? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Because of the general panic that was felt in the village, we started asking around. We wanted to -- we asked the headquarters what we should do, and the command of that battalion, they informed their superiors and that is the command of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade in Konjic and they asked them whether there was anything that could be done for the blockade to be lifted off the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said the blockade or the circle, was that a bit lower beyond the Sovicka Vrata, you said there was a block on the road, that there was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, that was the place some 1.5 to 2 kilometres below Sovicka Vrata.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Chamber knows already a lot about this place. I believe that they now recognise these names. Did you have any contacts with Bosniaks, Muslims or BH Army in Sovici and Doljani? Did you ask them what it was all about, what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: A gentleman from the battalion command contacted the commander of the army battalion in Sovici, Mr. Dzemal Orovic. I think that these two gentlemen were Stipe Pole and Juka Groznica. At the same time representatives of the BH Army from Jablanica came to us, Salih Jusic and Zajko Sihirlic, and they told us that there were no problems, that they did what they were supposed to do, and that we should not fear anything, that the blockade will be lifted. This was simply not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So this is 15. Did something special happen on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, the panic increased in the village. The people started getting ready to leave. At the same time, the number of armed provocations increased in the area of Kosna Luka, that is a village halfway between Doljani and Jablanica. The shooting increased in the mountains, there were an increased number of provocations by the members of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inform the superior command of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes. We were in constant contact with the Herceg Stjepan Brigade. We asked them to do something because every moment was crucial because the -- we were under a constant blockade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what did your neighbours, Muslims in Doljani, do? Did they help you? Did they assist you in any way? What was your relationship with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Throughout 1992 and throughout 1993, we -- the life in the village was absolutely normal and those relations were good, and nothing indicated that something like that could happen, but what surprised us was the fact that all the Muslim left Doljani in the night of the 16th and they all left towards Jablanica. On the following morning, we just saw the cattle roaming around, that all the villages in Doljani, all the houses in Doljani were empty, and that the -- our neighbours left towards Jablanica. This had a compounded our situation because we then realised that something was being prepared for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now is the time for a break. I have to interrupt you. I believe, Your Honours, that it is the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We left off with the 16th of April. Witness, did you want to say something else about that day, the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you were in touch with the Herceg Stjepan Brigade in Konjic and Mijat Tomic was one part of that brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes. We had regular information as to what was going on in the territory of Konjic municipality, i.e. what was going on in Trusinea and other villages. We had that information and that increased the panic in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that happened n which villages, and whose villages were those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Those were villages in the area of Klisa municipality, inhabited by Croats. A terrible massacre had taken place in those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
