utterances.text: Yes, before the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to the 17th. We said something about the 15th, the 16th. And on the 17th of April, 1993, I'm not going to interrupt you, just tell the Honourable Court what you know about that date, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: First of all, I said that we found out that in the course of the previous night, the Muslims had left Doljani village. This resulted in a huge panic in the morning hours of the 17th. On several occasions, we asked for the blockade to be lifted off. We saw, given the things that had happened in Konjic, given the provocations from Kosna Luka, we were afraid that we would have the same destiny as the villages in Konjic municipality, i.e. what happened to us on the 27th -- the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that what Cibo wanted to do with his policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the 17th and the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes. When things that happened in Konjic were supposed to happen in Doljani as well. However, the timely intervention of our Main Staff prevented that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned 20th --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: 28th. It did not happen then but it did happen on the 28th of July. What happened was that the Muslim forces from Jablanica stormed into Doljani, carried out the massacre of 36 civilians, took away about 250 civilians, women, children including, to the camp in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to private session because I need to something say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could we have the year he's talking about the 28th of July but we'd like to have the year as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we go to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying this because the Army of BH army intended to carry this out already in the month of April. With the arrival on the morning of the 17th, probably on the order of the Main Staff, the blockade started being lifted off Doljani and Sovici, shooting started in the surrounding -- in the neighbouring mountains and hills. We were in Doljani all that time, with the civilians and with our battalion, and all this stopped in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any -- was there any fighting in Kosna Luka, that is from Jablanica towards Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: All that time, there was -- Doljani was being shelled from mortars, there was shooting from the direction of Kosna Luka. However, in the village of Doljani, there were certain groups, although they thought that everybody had left Doljani, these groups were shooting and provoking throughout the day of the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the units which participated in the conflict in Sovici on the side of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Since the command of -- in Konjic was informed, and they in turn informed the Main Staff, and given the units that were there at the time, I believe that it could have been only Mr. Petkovic or the commander of the zone in charge of that area, and that is Mr. Mica Lasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the fighting stopped in the afternoon. Do you know when the fighting stopped in the afternoon? Did somebody surrender? How did this all end? In Sovici, I mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: The commander, Mr. Stipe Pole, the commander of Sovici, told me that the battalion commander, Dzemal Ovnovic had surrendered to him and then this commander was asked to order all the others, other members of the army, to surrender, because there was no further need for any fighting, because that is what the situation was and the situation was in favour of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me about the ratio of forces in Sovici and Doljani, the ratio of HVO forces vis-a-vis the BH Army forces that is before the conflict, until the 17th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Until the 17th, looking at the structure of the population, the ratio was 50-50. Looking at the entire local commune. In Sovici, there were about 70 per cent Muslims and 30 per cent Croats. This ratio was impaired for a very simple reason. Quite a number of Muslims from other municipalities came and settled in this village. I know some people from Jajce. Then members of the army came here from Prozor across the Baca hill. So in Sovici the ratio was 70-30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the ratio of soldiers, how many men did you have in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: We had about 150 to 170 men, because a large part of our soldiers had remained in Jablanica together with the civilians there. And according to my knowledge, the Sovici Battalion counted about 250 men, that is the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how many HVO soldiers were there on the 17th to the 18th? How many of the HVO troops were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: About 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: About 250.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Do you know what happened to members of the BH Army on the 17th, those who surrendered in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: According to what I know, a military police platoon took those soldiers to the military prison in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this military police platoon was in Doljani all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 17th of April, were all the members of the BH Army captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: No, because on the surrounding hills the fire still went on, and in the days that followed, some of the members of that BH Army surrendered to the military police. However, they stayed together with the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, please, do you have any knowledge upon whose orders? Military police took them to Ljubuski and when were they taken there, according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: According to what I know they were taken there around noon on the 17th and I presume they had been taken because they had been ordered by the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who physically drove them there? Was it military police again or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, it was the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on now to another topic. What happened to civilians? And please be quite open and quite straightforward. We have heard here all kinds of testimony so let us hear it from you. What happened to civilians in Sovici and Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: As for the civilians in Doljani, they left during the night. That part which stayed behind, because a certain part of them had stayed behind, they all gathered in the hamlet of Basici. Civilians from Sovici, by and large, gathered, they were looking where to put up, they wanted to be in one place, and they picked out the hamlet of Junuzovici because in a way it was outside the combat area and most of the civilians put up there and some of the civilians also went to the hamlet of Krkaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the school in Sovici, were there any civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: No, not in the Sovici school except later on the soldiers who surrendered and were also civilians in parts. They were in the school in Sovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us go whether anybody cared for them, did anybody guard them and who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I personally know, being the civilian HVO commander, I know that I did my utmost to provide those people with basic medical care, and I mean Dr. Vlado Luban, who regularly visited them, examined them. He is a physician who before the war was the director of the health centre, and all those civilians know him very well. He regularly -- they were regularly visited by Mr. Miroslav Juric, who is the President of the Catholic Charities Society, in case they were short of food or anything else. He attended to that, as far as I know, the civilians lived normally. It was the area of combat operations so they lived in fear but there was no harassment or anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you organise food for them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: They could go home without any problem whatsoever but since there were many troops in the village and all sorts of things, they preferred to be to keep together. They cooked their own food, as I said Mr. Juric visited them so that in case there were short of anything they would be supplied with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, your personal knowledge, did those civilians stay with you all the time or not? If not, when did they leave? Will you please tell the Court about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: After these conflicts, when the press service of the BH Army -- used it in the media and kept inciting the public saying that everything that moved in Sovici had been killed or burnt down, European monitors, UNPROFOR, I don't know, various other organisations they could come and see for themselves how the civilians were living. I know concretely of a visit of Mr. Petkovic and Sefer Halilovic, accompanied by Mr. Berislav Pusic, chairman of the exchange commission, representing Herceg-Bosna, and Hasan Rizvic, their representative of the army command from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Hasan Rizvic was, what was his office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: He was the commander of the army in Doljani and then when they moved to Jablanica he was made responsible for the exchange on behalf of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the date when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: No, I couldn't really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: All I know that during that contact we were told that those civilians had asked in view of all that was happening to be transferred to the territory held by the BH Army that is to Jablanica and that that be --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you may. Just slow down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: And that it be done, that is that they simply be transferred. And we asked or rather Minister Pusic that is what he told us later on he said that there would be no problem but he also requested that Croat civilians be released from Jablanica because they also wanted to get out, and there were about 600 of them. Further on, the Croats from Konjic and especially from the village of Radasina, where another massacre had taken place, they were also asking to be released. It was said that both requests would be met. And on the basis of that understanding, between Petkovic and Halilovic, and I believe it was in sometime in the beginning of May, that is on the 4th or the 5th of May, I can't say exactly those civilians were transferred or rather they were driven away to the territory controlled by, that is to Jablanica, that is to the territory controlled by the BH Army. However, the Croats from Jablanica were not allowed to do the same. And half of them ended up in prison later on and another half were sent to some labour platoons, subjected to particular torture for the duration of that, that is until the 1st of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please, I do not know if I understood you well. I'd like to clear this up for the Honourable Court. So you said that Petkovic and Halilovic agreed the exchange Berislav Pusic on behalf of the HZ HB, Hasan Rizic on behalf half of the BH Army and they agreed on the release of civilians. And the civilians in Sovici leave and the Croats never left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the operative officer responsible for the exchange? Was it Minister Pusic or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I don't know, I don't know, I guess it was he.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, let us move on to another subject and let us be very open about it. We have heard here about houses being put fire to, about mosques being damaged. So let us move into that area. Tell us, did the mosque in -- what happened to this mosque in Sovici? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: The mosque in Sovici and in Doljani was mined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mined? What do you mean mined?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Well, it means that it was demolished, that explosives were planted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean dynamite?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, I mean dynamite. At night. We requested the military police and others to investigate and establish who had done it because that was a crime. And we are ashamed of that to this day. We still feel the shame. The military police conducted an investigation but I personally never learned who had done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: That was on the 18th or maybe 19th or the 17th I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us 18th, 17th or perhaps 18th to 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And what happened to houses? Were they indeed torched? What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: The houses were by and large set on fire. After all these happenings, towards the end of 1993, Muslim houses were also set on fire but not all of them and Croat houses too, in a large part of these hamlets one could say that most of the villages were burnt down. The houses were torched during the operations themselves, that is in the course of the operations, the houses were destroyed and burnt, and a large number of houses were also torched later on during those operations. Who did that, I cannot know of any personal knowledge but I know that it was out of any control and we were really decisively against it resolutely against that, but naturally the troops came from all over it was impossible for us, like civilian commander under the command of a small battalion, we could not prevent it, we could not put an end to that, but I can tell you that it was beyond any control, but nevertheless there are some Muslim houses in Doljani which were never torched but I must also say that a number of them were torched after the 27th, 28th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You year you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: 1993. And after this massacre in Doljani, a certain knowledge that we gained and that we received --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then a large number of houses were burnt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: They were burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the civilians after the 27th, that is in Sovici and Doljani, did they stay there or did they leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: The civilians in Doljani, I have already said they were all taken to the museum in Jablanica and from Sovici they simply moved out towards West Herzegovina or Croatia or wherever they could be accommodated, so that the village practically remained empty with nobody but troops in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now I'd like to ask you to move towards conclusion. Are you aware that members of -- if the members of the Convicts Battalion were in Sovici and Doljani between the 17th, 18th, 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I know that in the operations, soldiers from Tomislavgrad participated, also from Posusje, Siroki, that there were ATG groups which practically -- were not in Sovici itself. They went along the edges of the village to positions held by the army, to neutralise those positions, because fire was coming from there, and that is the area above Sovici, Pasije Stijene for instance, Bacina, Pisvir, all the way to Kosna Luka because our principal objective was to establish a defence line facing Jablanica because that is where the village was -- where the thrust of the attack against the village came from. So that from what I know, and from the command, these ATGs did not come down to the village of Sovici itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see them in Kosna Luka? Will you tell the Honourable Court how did they get to Kosna Luka which way did they take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Well, as I have said they followed on the edge, Pasije Stijene, Bacina, Pomen, Pisvir, 904 feature, that is also Tovarnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be easier for you I have a photographer here this is Exhibit 8.2 and we could perhaps show it and perhaps you could point at those mountains and which route did they take to come down to Kosna Luka? And perhaps it could be put on the ELMO and you will show us then. You keep on talking until we get the signal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: They climbed down between features 902 and 904, between Tovarnica and they took that road between these two hills to come down to Kosna Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we have got it on, take this pointer show us which road that they took to come down to Kosna Luka

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's still on not. We're waiting and we'll come back to this. Tell me, did you see Mr. Naletilic in Doljani and Sovici or Sovici, if yes, when and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Naletilic in the afternoon, in the evening on the 19th, in front of the command in Doljani. When he came with two or three of his men, since I was the commander of the civilian part of the HVO and Stipe Pole, as the military commander, and that was the first time that I met Mr. Mladen Naletilic. However, that day, some very regrettable things happened that day, that is that day practically three soldiers, members of that ATG group were killed, and Mr. Naletilic, from what I know, was there only briefly and he said that he had to go back in order to prepare for the funeral of those three members of that ATG group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, but it -- very briefly because he was with his men and he said that he was very sorry, as far as I can remember, that one soldier was Boka, and he was his neighbour and he said he simply had to go to his family in Siroki and he left that command in no time. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the ATGs? Did they leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, they left, those who had been with him but as far as I can remember, Mr. Cikota stayed on at the feature, at that Tovarnica, because he was to reinforce the positions facing Jablanica together with our home guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those ATGs ever come back to Sovici or Doljani after the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go into private session, please? And we shall wait for the ELMO to work, but then will you use the marker and draw the route which the ATGs took and my last question but can we go into private session? And then I will turn you over to my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ATG groups took this edge of the village on the other side is the Pomeli municipality and the Muslims had taken this whole part of the hill. Pasije Stijene, and Bacina Mount for a simple reason and I absolutely must tell it, in order to control the village of Doljani, and Ravno hydro power plant as the principal power generating facility. It was their strategic goal. It wasn't only that they wanted to take the village, so they had deployed their forces on the Bacina Mountain, Pomen, Oklanice, Pisvir is behind there and all this way here, so the ATG group moved in that direction, this is where 904 feature is, here is 902, and between them in Tovarnica where they climbed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, wait now in Tovarnica just draw an arrow, an arrow down pointing at Doljani, just do that and telling us which date was it when they climbed down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: It was on the 20th of April, and before that, before they descended -- before that descent the leader of that ATG group, Cikota, was killed and he had our home guards with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did these ATGs come down from the mountain to Kosna Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: To Kosna Luke? On the 19th, except that on the 19th they came down on the 19th, and when they came down it was then that Boka was killed and Cikota stayed behind, that is up in the hills, with the home guards, in order to reinforce the line and he was killed on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have this marker. Take the black marker and just draw an arrow from Tovarnica to Kosna Luka.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much and just the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could our honourable Madam Registrar give the documents to the witness at the same time. D1/392, 393, 394, 395, 396, and 397?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, everybody warns me and I was really in the wrong too. Will you please slow down? Everybody warns me. You do not have to read these documents, will you just cast a look at those documents? Don't read through them because these documents are self explanatory and if you are reading any of them, then tell us now I'm reading document such and such because you have a number down there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I'm talking about documents D1/392 tell us are you familiar with that document or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: D1/393. I'm familiar with it. Document D1/394.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could I just ask, what does it mean if the witness says, "I'm familiar with the document"? Could he give some more explanation other than saying he's familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just say what is it that you're familiar with, the incident described, the document itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: No, no, no. I mean I know about the incidents that described here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes, when I say that I'm familiar with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please give us the document, the number of the document and the date? I think that every document must bear a signature somewhere.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: So the document D1/394 [RealTime transcript read in error "D1/354"], the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know. The document, the transcript is wrong because it says 354, it should be 394.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes. Document D1/395 of the 23rd of March, 1993. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: No, I don't. Document D1/396, 11th of January, 1993, yes, I'm aware of the problem that the document refers to. And document D1/397, of the 19th of January, 1993, no, I'm not aware of it, but now that I read this, I see that it reflected the reality on the ground. And what happened at the time, and how they were getting ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And now let's go to documents of the Prosecution, 362 and 360. These are orders issued by Mr. Milivoj Petkovic. Will you please have a look at them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very glad to say that this document has been translated into French, Your Honour, Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Document 4 of May, 1993, yes, I'm familiar with it. And document 362, dating 5 of May, 1993, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for coming here and I hope that you have assisted this Chamber in getting a complete picture of the events. I have finished, Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, we still have 15 minutes to go. At the beginning of the direct examination, Mr. Krsnik asked for a short break before the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tomorrow. The meeting is tomorrow, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you, Witness, whether you are ready to continue for another 15 minutes for cross-examination by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos. We have to stop at quarter to 2.00 sharply.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness NN, I will call you Witness NN as you are a protective witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P2 and Exhibit P906 which are two maps? I'll also provide the exhibits which I intends to use for the cross-examination of this witness. If I could ask the usher to put Exhibit P2 the map, if it's there on the overhead projector, please? P2. If I can assist the registry, we have a copy here of Exhibit P2. The other exhibit which I will need shortly is Exhibit P906. If this map could be pleased placed on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, witness, in front of you you have some of the municipalities in Herzegovina, and I'd like to focus on the municipality of Jablanica which is the topic of discussion here today, so I don't know if we can focus out a bit. That's fine. Please stop. Now, Witness, is it correct that the municipality of Jablanica is strategically a very important municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the reasons why it's such an important strategic important municipality is that the two main roads which go up north to Bosnia and to Sarajevo run through this municipality? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it also true that the major power stations of Bosnia-Herzegovina are actually found in this municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: In addition to elsewhere, there are also some in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the major power stations are in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there are power stations in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: There is one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is that power station? Could you indicate it on the map here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: It is in Jablanica itself. In the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we now place Exhibit 906 on the overhead projector? Now, witness, this is a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina which indicates all the municipalities, and the municipalities indicated in the red colour or orange colour are the municipalities which consist -- which consisted the territory of Herceg-Bosna as it was founded on the 18th of November, 1991. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really don't know whether this is the Prosecutor's tactic to prevent me from finishing with my witnesses. I believe that I've followed your guidelines. I have followed your instructions closely. I was very specific. I did not go outside 1993, whereas my learned friend starts with the map of HZ HB and the 11th of November, 1991. This is my objection, and please decide, and I always trust your wisdom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we believe this question is related to this case, and we'll see where Mr. Bos will lead us, and if he is going to -- somewhere far away, we'll stop him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, my question was, does the area indicated in orange reflect the territory of Herceg-Bosna as it was founded in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I can say for Jablanica, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it true, Witness NN, that Jablanica also fell in one of the cantons as it was assigned to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, one of the canton that is was assigned to the Bosnian Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Witness, wouldn't you agree with me that although the majority of the population in Jablanica was Muslim, that this municipality was very important for the Bosnian Croats to gain control because of its strategic position and because of its resources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: It was very important for anybody, because of its position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's for now for the maps. Now, Witness, at the end of your examination-in-chief you were shown a few documents by the Defence and I would just like to have you to have another look at Exhibit D1/397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My witness has looked at me when the Prosecutor said Bosnian Croats. I kindly ask my learned friend not to say Bosnian Croat. They are Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina. There is no such thing a thing as a Bosnian Croat, so can my learned friend address the witness in that way and use that term? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems that we have already arrived at agreement on using of the terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have Exhibit D1/397 in front of you? I think you do. Let me just -- upon asking to comment on this document, you said that this document reflected the reality on the ground. Is that correct? Is that what you testified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: I testified and said that the BH Army, all the time prepared itself in order to cleanse Jablanica of Croats and to destroy the HVO and I testified that this document corroborates the fact that this was done systematically and in a coordinated manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Witness NN, if you testified that -- if you talk about cleansing it seems to me that you're talking about offensive actions and if you just look at paragraph 2 of this document, which reads as follows: "The BH Army units in the area of Jablanica and Konjic, SO, should be in full combat readiness and prepared for persistent defence in case of attack." So this paragraph talks about defensive actions rather than offensive actions, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in Jablanica, we were a very small ethnic group and not for a single moment did we build our defence in order to attack. This is just ridiculous, farcical, that we could do anything in Jablanica municipality where we were less than 10 per cent. There were about 2.000 of us and about 20.000 Muslims and for us to be preparing for an attack was practically impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Isn't it true that HVO troops outside the municipality could actually move into the municipality and assist the HVO? And if you look at paragraph 5 of this same document, it says, "Prevents movements, regrouping or advance by HVO units from other municipalities in your zone of responsibility." Isn't that exactly what happened, Witness NN?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN
utterances.text: In the area of Jablanica municipality, there were no other HVO forces, just the Mijat Tomic Battalion until the moment we asked for the area to be deblocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to move to a different topic so maybe this is a good time to end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, I'm afraid that we have to keep you for another day. We will continue tomorrow morning. You have to understand that you're still under the oath so during your stay in The Hague, do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we will rise until tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
